entry.title: DeCompCert: A Verified Decompiler for CompCert-Generated AArch64. DeCompCert is a Rocq-verified decompiler for AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert.
entry.summary:
DeCompCert is a Rocq-verified decompiler for AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert. It reconstructs CompCert C through nine reverse passes, combining deductively verified transformations with translation validation. Untrusted OCaml and Datalog analyses propose candidate reconstructions, while verified validators accept only candidates that satisfy the required semantic correspondence.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #cryptography #rust

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Shuffling is Universal: Statistical Additive Randomized Encodings for All Functions
entry.summary:
The shuffle model is a widely used abstraction for non-interactive anonymous communication. It allows $n$ parties holding private inputs $x_1,\dots,x_n$ to simultaneously send messages to an evaluator, so that the messages are received in a random order. The evaluator can then compute a joint function $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)$, ideally while learning nothing else about the private inputs.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics
